newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Leumi okays sale of Africa Israel stake.
newsitem.headline: Leumi okays sale of Africa Israel stake.

text.p: Bank Leumi's board of directors on Sunday approved the sale of a controlling stake in its subsidiary Africa Israel Investments to Israeli businessman Lev Leviev.

Leviev, one of Israel's leading diamond exporters, will pay $190 million for 46.58 percent of equity and 54.2 percent of voting rights in the company. The price values Africa Israel, shorn of its insurance business, at $400 million, Leumi said in a statement.

Leumi, which received two formal bids in a tender for the stake, must lower its holdings in Africa Israel to 25 percent by the end of this year to comply with banking reform that requires Israeli banks to reduce their non-banking assets.

Banking law further requires that Leumi later reduce its Africa Israel stake to 20 percent. Leviev has agreed to give Leumi an option to sell him an additional five percent based on the same company valuation.
Leviev has given Leumi another option to sell him the rest of its Africa Israel holdings within 3.5 years at a price based on a company valuation of $340 million.
The agreement is expected to be signed in the coming days, the statement said.

Africa Israel is a leading holding concern with interests in real estate, construction, tourism and hotels. Its insurance holdings are being spun off separately and sold to Italian insurer Generali SpA.
Leumi is Israel's second biggest bank.
